issues.legal_issue: An enactment invalidated as void from its inception does not repeal an earlier enactment that remained in force.
material_facts: An earlier law had abolished the inams and vested them in the State before a later law purported to repeal it.
The High Court struck down the later law because the inams had already vested and the later law’s effect was to deprive inamdars of compensation secured under the earlier law.
The State did not appeal against the decision striking down the later law.
issues.conclusion: The earlier abolition laws remained in force; the invalidated later law did not repeal them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the later enactment as non est and void from its inception, relying on Deep Chand v. State of Uttar Pradesh. It distinguished B. N. Tiwari v. Union of India, where an earlier administrative rule had been cancelled by its replacement before the replacement was invalidated; here the later enactment could not undo the effect already achieved under the earlier laws.

rule.if: civil_appeal_after_later_law_invalidated and later_law_purported_to_repeal_prior_law and prior_law_had_already_effected_vesting and later_law_was_invalidated_as_void_from_inception

predicates.civil_appeal_after_later_law_invalidated: A civil appeal concerns the continuing effect of an earlier law after a later law purporting to repeal it was invalidated.
predicates.later_law_purported_to_repeal_prior_law: The legislature enacted a later law that purported to repeal an earlier law.
predicates.prior_law_had_already_effected_vesting: The earlier law had already transferred the relevant property or rights to the State before the later law was enacted.
predicates.later_law_was_invalidated_as_void_from_i: A court invalidated the later law as void from its inception because it attempted to undo a legal position already established under the earlier law.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns this sequence and the later repealing law was void from its inception after the earlier law had already effected vesting, the earlier law remains in force.

issues.legal_issue: Rights to income and benefits attached to inam land, including the relevant abkari rights, vest with the land when the inam is abolished unless expressly saved.
material_facts: The grant covered the inam lands with all sources of income, including rights relating to liquor-shop fees and benefits from trees.
The rights to tap trees and receive tree-related fees concerned trees standing on the land, and the relevant income rights were granted as part of the inam rather than independently of it.
The abolition law provided for the vesting of rights, title and interests in the inam land, subject to rights expressly saved by the law.
issues.conclusion: The abkari rights were part of the inam and vested in the State along with the land.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(1)(c), 2(2), and 3(1) and 3(2)(b) of the Hyderabad Inams Abolition Act, 1955, the Act’s undefined terms take their meaning from the specified related enactments, and rights, title and interests in inam land vest in the State unless expressly saved. Section 2(1-b) of the Andhra Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1317 Fasli defines land to include benefits pertaining to land and things attached to it. The Court relied on State of Bihar v. Rameshwar Pratap Narain Singh, which treated a right appurtenant to ownership of land as an interest in the estate.

rule.if: civil_appeal_on_scope_of_land_abolition and grant_included_all_sources_of_income and benefits_were_attached_to_or_appurtenant_to_land and vesting_law_transferred_interests_in_land and rights_were_not_expressly_saved

predicates.civil_appeal_on_scope_of_land_abolition: A civil appeal concerns whether rights associated with land were included in its abolition and transfer to the State.
predicates.grant_included_all_sources_of_income: The grant described the land as carrying all sources of income rather than granting the disputed income rights independently.
predicates.benefits_were_attached_to_or_appurtenant: The disputed benefits arose from trees, uses, or other features attached to the land or were otherwise appurtenant to its ownership.
predicates.vesting_law_transferred_interests_in_lan: The law provided for the transfer to the State of rights and interests in the land when it was abolished.
predicates.rights_were_not_expressly_saved: The law did not expressly preserve the disputed rights from the transfer.

issues.definition: When an abolition appeal concerns rights granted with the land, those rights are attached or appurtenant to it, and the law transfers land interests without saving them, the rights vest with the land.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation payable for abolition of an inam includes compensation for abkari rights that form part of the inam.
material_facts: The abkari rights were granted as part of the inam and vested in the State with the inam land.
The abolition law prescribed compensation for the inam as a whole through a formula based on the interests and income specified by the law.
issues.conclusion: The compensation payable for the abolished inam included the abkari rights vested with it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Hyderabad Inams Abolition Act, 1955 provides for compensation payable to the inamdar for the inams abolished under section 3. Because the abkari rights were part of the inam and vested with it, the Court held that the compensation provided under section 12 included those rights.

predicates.appeal_concerns_compensation_for_abolish: An appeal concerns the compensation payable when a landholding is abolished and transferred to the State.
predicates.disputed_rights_formed_part_of_landholdi: The disputed rights were granted as part of the landholding and transferred with it.
predicates.compensation_scheme_applied_to_landholdi: The compensation scheme calculated compensation for the abolished landholding rather than treating each associated right as a separate acquisition.

issues.definition: When rights formed part of an abolished landholding and the compensation scheme covers that holding as a whole, compensation includes those rights.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation scheme for abolishing inams as an agrarian reform is not invalid merely because it does not provide separate compensation for abkari rights forming part of the inam.
material_facts: The abkari rights formed part of the inam and were included in the compensation payable for its abolition.
The abolition legislation was intended to carry out agrarian reforms by making land available to persons without land.
The appellant challenged the compensation arrangement as inadequate because it did not separately compensate the abkari rights.
issues.conclusion: The compensation scheme could not be challenged on that ground because the abolition legislation gave effect to agrarian reforms.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A of the Constitution protects legislation providing for acquisition by the State of an estate or rights in it, or for extinguishment or modification of such rights, from challenge under Article 31(2). The Court relied on B. Shankara Rao Badani v. State of Mysore, which applied that protection to legislation undertaken as agrarian reform.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_abolition_co: A party challenges the compensation scheme for a State abolition of property or property rights.
predicates.law_carried_out_agrarian_reform: The law was enacted to carry out agrarian reform by making land available to persons without land.
predicates.disputed_rights_were_included_in_overall: The disputed rights formed part of the abolished estate and were covered by the overall compensation scheme, even though no separate amount was provided for them.

issues.definition: When an abolition-compensation challenge concerns a law carrying out agrarian reform and the disputed rights are covered by the overall compensation scheme, that scheme is protected from the challenge.
